author: partner-desk
title: Vantro backs grassroots footy grounds in regional Victoria
dek: A three-year program funds lighting and change rooms at twelve community grounds.
body:
Vantro has announced a three-year program funding ground improvements at twelve community football clubs in regional Victoria. The money will pay for new lighting and accessible change rooms. This partner piece explains how the clubs were chosen and the conditions Vantro has attached to the program.

What the program funds

Many regional clubs train under old lights that make evening sessions unsafe in winter, and change rooms that were built before women's and junior football grew. The program targets both.

  • Lighting: LED training lights at eight grounds, allowing safer sessions after dark and lower power bills.
  • Change rooms: accessible, gender-neutral facilities at six grounds, including two that receive both upgrades.
  • Maintenance: a fund for repairs during the three years, managed by the clubs.

Work at the first four grounds is planned for the off-season, before training starts next year.

How clubs were chosen

Vantro says the clubs were selected with their local leagues, based on need and community use rather than on the size of the club. Each league nominated grounds where facilities were holding back participation, particularly for women's, girls' and junior teams. The final list was agreed with the leagues and published by them.

RegionGroundsMain upgrade
Goulburn Valley4Lighting
Gippsland3Change rooms
Western District3Lighting
Wimmera2Both

No betting promotion at junior games

Vantro has committed that no betting promotion will run at junior matches at any of the twelve grounds. Its logo will appear on a plaque at each upgraded facility, but not on junior uniforms, junior match-day signage or club communications aimed at children.

The clubs keep full control of their own sponsorship arrangements. Vantro says it will not ask clubs to promote its betting products in exchange for the funding.

Why a bookmaker funds community sport

Gambling sponsorship of sport is an active public debate in Australia, and many people are uncomfortable with betting brands near junior sport. Vantro says the conditions above are designed to keep the program about facilities rather than marketing. Clubs and leagues will report on how the facilities are used each season.

The takeaway

Twelve regional grounds will get better lights and change rooms over three years, with no betting promotion at junior games. If your club is one of them, the league will share timelines directly.

Gambling is for adults only. If betting is causing problems for you or someone close to you, free and confidential support is available from Gambling Help Online on 1800 858 858.
